title: Dance music and halls in New Orleans
summary: He played with Fields and Planchet for club dances, at halls like Francs Amis.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I've already interviewed him. He's a wonderful man. He plays guitar. He's really a fine fellow. And we enjoy seeing him. I was going to ask again about... I know you never did much in the dance music in your early days, but do you remember much about the dance music that you heard in New Orleans? Any of the big balls or even carnival balls or other kind of... Oh, gosh, yes.

Yes, because I played... I played with a... Even while I was studying classic side, I played with an orchestra there named Fields and Planchet. And that was the popular combination for most of the club dancers. And I did quite a bit of playing with them.
Do you remember any of the clubs that you played for, the halls?

Well, I remember... Well, there's one hall there, which was the popular hall for club dancers. It was called... It was French name, Frans Amis. Yes. And I can't remember the other hall, but there were two halls that were the popular halls for club dancers. We did. Perseverance.
We did. Oh. Oh. Good. That's working all right. You can get about a half hour on each side of that.
